docs.title: ai-rulez is the opt-in single source for agent instructions, with the prose in shared macros
docs.text:
Id: e1545d12-ac20-426b-9cd5-519e80a56b5f Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-035 (docs/adr/035-ai-rulez-as-the-agent-instruction-source.md), §1 and §5; issue #309 Revisit when: a host stops reading its generated file, ai-rulez leaves PyPI, or a sixth host is expected to open PRs See: repo-setup.md#a-resume-driven-repo-setup-skill-reads-check-blocks-from-the-setup-doc-no-separate-manifest — 68ac4665-dcde-456b-aef7-2faaf6fe51f4 — as of 2026-10-11 See: template-testing.md#collection-literals-are-rendered-through-one-shared-macro — 47b21a49-5fc4-46b8-b450-7d9f3225706c — as of 2026-10-11

include_ai_rulez (default off, full preset) with an ai_rulez_presets multiselect renders .ai-rulez/ sources from which ai-rulez generates each host's native instruction files and skill copies. With the toggle off, the hand-written AGENTS.md and the Claude-only skills render. The section prose lives once in _macros.jinja; both the hand-written file and the rule sources call the same macros. The pin lives in its own agents dependency group, exact, Renovate-tracked through the native uv manager.

Reason: the generated project's branch-name check already whitelists five agent prefixes, but only Claude received the repo-setup skill and only two hosts received instructions; hand-writing five formats is the duplication the template exists to remove. ai-rulez ships on PyPI (no Node) and has the cobo shape — sources in, committed output out, a check that proves they agree. A second hand-maintained copy of the paragraphs would recreate inside the template the drift it removes downstream. Its own group because dev includes style wholesale and only two callers invoke the tool; upstream's pre-commit hooks would add a second rev pin. The exact pin matters because the PyPI launcher downloads a Go binary and proceeds with a warning if the checksum file cannot be fetched.

Rejected alternative: hand-written per-host files — five dialects drifting.

docs.title: Generated host files are build output; the template renders none of them
docs.text:
Id: e827d3fc-e3f6-4852-b2e3-d56180eac949 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-035 §2 and §8 (docs/adr/035-ai-rulez-as-the-agent-instruction-source.md) Revisit when: ai-rulez and copier produce identical bytes for the same content, or the template gains a post-render step See: agent-instructions.md#ai-rulez-is-the-opt-in-single-source-for-agent-instructions-with-the-prose-in-shared-macros — e1545d12-ac20-426b-9cd5-519e80a56b5f — as of 2026-10-11 See: template-updates.md#copieryml-defines-no-_tasks — 86130379-1660-4992-8aba-8b6cd7b4a9f7 — as of 2026-10-11

The template renders .ai-rulez/ and stops. AGENTS.md, the Copilot instructions and the per-host skill copies are written by the adopter's first ai-rulez generate and committed from then on. Turning the toggle on via update leaves a project with no instruction files until the generator runs (the after-update message names the two commands; CI is red until the output is committed). Turning it off requires running ai-rulez's clean command before the update, while the sources it reads still exist, because the host files are not copier-managed and would otherwise stay committed and stale.

Reason: copier's renderer and ai-rulez's renderer produce different bytes for the same content (ai-rulez composes its own headings and stamps a provenance header with a content hash), so rendering both would diff on first generate and every copier update would re-render on top of generated files — churn on files the adopter never touched. As build output they sit outside the 3-way merge, which then covers only the small per-rule sources. Neither direction is automatic because the template has no tasks. Dropping the toggle from full was rejected: full means every toggle, and a preset that quietly omits one is a worse surprise than a loud one.

Rejected alternative: render the generated files as well — the churn above.

docs.title: No builtin ai-rulez domains, and ai-rulez never touches .gitignore
docs.text:
Id: e9823c4a-891f-4344-8d64-029dd8d31138 Type: decision Type: constraint Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-035 §3–4 (docs/adr/035-ai-rulez-as-the-agent-instruction-source.md) Revisit when: a builtin domain stops contradicting a gate the project enforces, or the gitignore stops being cobo-sealed See: gitignore-generation.md#cobo-generates-the-gitignore-with-a-hash-sealed-fence-and-lockfiles — 3e3bc38e-bc1e-4e65-b74d-e91848262157 — as of 2026-10-11

builtins = false: the shipped rules are only the project's own. gitignore = false: the generated output is committed and ai-rulez does not rewrite the ignore file.

Reason: every one of the seven auto-included builtin domains either restates a gate or contradicts it — complexity 20 versus ruff's 5, 120 columns versus 88, 80% coverage versus 99%, "use conventional commits" versus the blocking title check. A rule an agent obeys and a gate that fails it must never be two separately maintained sentences, and per-domain exclusions would leave the next release free to add a contradiction to a domain opted into. Off entirely also keeps the generated file ~60 lines instead of ~270. ai-rulez's default gitignore rewrite would break the cobo-sealed fence and hide the very files GitHub must find in the repository.

Rejected alternative: per-domain ! exclusions — the next-release risk.

docs.title: Two gates plus a convergence scenario over every host
docs.text:
Id: b23fd420-5b88-4075-93ad-5122b4f7622e Type: decision Type: incident Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-035 §6–7 (docs/adr/035-ai-rulez-as-the-agent-instruction-source.md) Revisit when: ai-rulez gains a check mode for preset output, or a host's generated output changes format See: template-testing.md#generated-files-must-be-formatter-canonical-not-merely-valid — 9b931598-7e52-4ff1-bb07-ef65c01d5369 — as of 2026-10-11 See: lint-orchestration.md#the-tox-style-env-is-the-sole-authoritative-lint-suite-prek-is-a-fast-gate-not-a-second-suite — 9b74fc8b-a808-4f2b-bdbd-9e4253c1b35a — as of 2026-10-11

prek runs the generator as a fixing hook; tox style runs ai-rulez validate; and ci.yml's hooks job additionally fails on any working-tree change including untracked files. A template-ci scenario renders the toggle on with every offered host, runs the generator, then the generated project's own fixing hooks, and gates on git diff; it also runs the checking hooks and gates on their exit codes. Checking hooks skip the paths a generator owns (.continue/prompts/ for trailing-whitespace, yamllint and the editorconfig checker; .mdc for the editorconfig checker), rendered only under the toggle.

Reason: there is no check mode for preset output, and a fixing hook only fails on a modified tracked file — a project that never committed its output would have it regenerated untracked and stay green, shipping instructions that exist on no branch. Two generators writing one tree that disagree on a byte leave a repository that never converges. The defaults emit markdown alone and converge; two hosts found only once the scenario covered every host do not — continue-dev's YAML header carries trailing-space comment lines the whitespace hook strips and the next generate restores, and cursor's .mdc rules fail the editorconfig checker because the \.md$ exclude does not reach the extra character. A checking hook rejecting generated output cannot be satisfied at all, so it gets the .copier-answers.yml answer: skip the generator-owned path.

Consequence: the width of the gate is the width of the output it sees; every offered host widens the scenario that must keep passing.

docs.title: No CLAUDE.md by default; claude left the preset defaults; gemini is no longer offered
docs.text:
Id: 1a6849be-72d0-4990-abe2-7a0243cd5e67 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-035, 2026-10 amendment (docs/adr/035-ai-rulez-as-the-agent-instruction-source.md) Revisit when: Claude Code stops reading AGENTS.md natively, or the maintainers start using Gemini See: agent-instructions.md#ai-rulez-is-the-opt-in-single-source-for-agent-instructions-with-the-prose-in-shared-macros — e1545d12-ac20-426b-9cd5-519e80a56b5f — as of 2026-10-11

The default shape uses AGENTS.md alone, including for Claude Code. The former @AGENTS.md wrapper is neither rendered nor preserved on update any more, so an update deletes leftover copies (customized ones too). ai_rulez_presets defaults to codex and copilot; claude is still offered but not default; gemini was removed from the choices.

Reason: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md natively, removing the only reason the wrapper existed — and a leftover CLAUDE.md makes Claude Code's default mode skip AGENTS.md, the opposite of what the default shape wants. The codex host already writes AGENTS.md, so claude only added a duplicate wrapper and a .claude/ tree. The maintainers do not use Gemini and every offered host widens the convergence scenario.

Rejected alternative: keep excluding CLAUDE.md from updates to protect adopter guidance — kept a file that actively harmed the default; the README tells adopters to move unique guidance first, and git history keeps the old content.

Consequence: by default the per-host skills no longer reach Claude Code, which looks under .claude/skills/; adopters who want them select claude. Removing a choice has a sharp edge: a --defaults update (what Renovate runs) silently replaces a recorded selection containing a removed choice with the new defaults, so a project that selected gemini loses every other host too and keeps a stale GEMINI.md; such a project cleans before updating and re-selects.

docs.title: One exhaustive import-linter layers contract: cli above independent components above core above utils
docs.text:
Id: 3b7cdbee-7c66-4e52-9d7e-8ab0ffe32e56 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-014 (docs/adr/014-import-linter-for-architecture-contracts.md) Revisit when: core starts importing utils, a second orchestrator component appears, or a component needs an exception the layers model cannot express See: components.md#secondary-components-are-subcommands-of-one-console-root-not-separate-scripts — 3d60ab14-8ff9-47db-b326-d7e82947a6cf — as of 2026-10-11

import-linter is an always-on style tool. A single layers contract stacks cli (present only with include_cli), the enabled non-CLI components as pipe-separated independent siblings, then core, then utils. The contract is exhaustive, so any subpackage not named in the layers breaks it; non-layer foundations (__main__, __metadata__, _version, _c_extension) are listed as exhaustive ignores.

Reason: components are gated on toggles and meant to be independent — a web -> gui import is a latent bug against a sibling that may not be installed — and none of the existing tools enforce which module may import which. Sibling semantics give independence, layer order gives layering, and a separate cli layer captures its legitimate lazy-import orchestration without ignore rules. Exhaustiveness closes the gap that motivated the tool: coding agents and hurried humans add a top-level package (data/, marketplace/) that an unlisted-is-unconstrained contract ignored; prose in the agent instructions does not hold, a failing style run does. utils below core matches current reality and the conventional leaf-helpers model.

Rejected alternative: separate independence plus layers contracts — redundant, and independence is degenerate with zero or one component, whereas the single contract degrades to a valid core > utils.

Consequence: the contract is Jinja-conditional on enabled components, so a component's coverage is exercised only when it is generated; the one boundary it cannot forbid (cli importing MCP or worker) is harmless because cli legitimately sits on top.

docs.title: Whole-program analyzers are local system hooks backed by the style group
docs.text:
Id: 41f3397d-1afb-4e57-a0bd-b5ef85089bfc Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-014 §4 (docs/adr/014-import-linter-for-architecture-contracts.md); the same delivery is recorded for basedpyright in ADR-005 and sphinx-lint in ADR-011 Revisit when: prek gains a way to run repo hooks with the project installed, or the fast gate becomes too slow See: lint-orchestration.md#the-tox-style-env-is-the-sole-authoritative-lint-suite-prek-is-a-fast-gate-not-a-second-suite — 9b74fc8b-a808-4f2b-bdbd-9e4253c1b35a — as of 2026-10-11

import-linter and slotscheck (like basedpyright, mypy and sphinx-lint) run on the prek gate as local language = "system" hooks that shell through uv run --locked --group style, and in the tox style env from the same group. Neither uses the upstream repo hook the tool ships.

Reason: both need the installed package and a whole-import-graph build (grimp) or an import of every module (slotscheck). prek runs a repo hook in its own isolated venv with only the hook's own deps, so the project is not installed there and the graph cannot be built. A local system hook sees the project's real environment, uses the single style pin (no second rev for Renovate), and verified end-to-end that an injected upward import fails the hook. slotscheck is worth the fast gate because it checks a property nothing else covers; the redundant type checkers ty/pyrefly/zuban stay style-env-only so five type checkers do not stack on every commit.

Rejected alternative: style-env-only for import-linter — an earlier revision of the record, on the imprecise premise that prek cannot install the package; true of the isolated repo-hook pattern, not of the local system hook.

docs.title: Network-dependent checks run on a weekly cron, never in the merge gate
docs.text:
Id: 3e5b9525-9087-4125-b19f-80f6c226c01f Type: decision Type: constraint Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-011 (docs/adr/011-docs-linting-and-cross-platform-filename-safety.md), ADR-012 §4 (docs/adr/012-cobo-for-gitignore-generation.md), ADR-031 §3 (docs/adr/031-single-render-entrypoint.md); the same posture is cited for check-security.yml's periodic scans Revisit when: a network-dependent check becomes reliable enough to block, or the merge gate gains a retry mechanism

Checks whose outcome depends on the network or on an upstream that can change without a commit here — docs link checking, the cobo gitignore drift check, the template's generated-artifact drift check — run on a weekly schedule plus workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request, and never join the check aggregation. They surface rot as a visible, non-blocking workflow result; a tox env or mise task lets a maintainer run each on demand.

Reason: a transient 5xx, a rate limit, a site blocking CI, or an upstream boilerplate update must never block an unrelated merge. A weekly signal is the right cadence for drift that accumulates slowly, and a PR-time check cannot see drift caused by something that changed underneath the repository.

Rejected alternative: run them on pull requests — flaky red checks on unrelated changes.

docs.title: A single union coverage gate across the whole matrix
docs.text:
Id: ca90a48d-f648-40b3-ae1a-05f9f21cf411 Type: decision Status: superseded Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-026 §1 (docs/adr/026-combined-cross-matrix-coverage-and-tokenless-html-host.md) Superseded by: 467b6cc3-775b-4e4c-9a8e-b0d1c3d733ac See: testing-strategy.md#coverage-exclusions-are-per-site-pragmas-and-the-globs-must-match-the-installed-layout — 68366ce3-cc8e-4720-aa91-5eb83aaf2e2d — as of 2026-10-11

Each matrix cell combined its per-interpreter data, kept a non-gating report, and uploaded a per-OS artifact; one coverage-combine job (today's coverage-report) merged every cell and was the only place fail_under = 99 was enforced, measuring the union of all OS and interpreter cells. relative_files = true made data from different runners mergeable, complementing the src/site-packages path remap. The combined XML became the one Codecov upload.

Reason: per-cell gating measured each OS alone, so a line covered on Linux but gated off on Windows was reported inconsistently, and there was no authoritative cross-fan-out number. The union is the correct scope. This held while the matrix was symmetric — every cell measured the same code.

Consequence: once the CI job split into path-filtered per-component jobs, a skipped component dropped its subtree from the union and the single gate failed on every partial PR; the principle survives per component in the successor.

docs.title: A tokenless public HTML coverage mirror via smokeshow
docs.text:
Id: 21119a10-df03-494b-ac84-a57b9b1832c2 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-026 §2 (docs/adr/026-combined-cross-matrix-coverage-and-tokenless-html-host.md) Revisit when: Codecov becomes tokenless for private repositories, or smokeshow changes its rate-limit model See: external-integrations.md#a-freshly-generated-project-is-green-on-first-push-with-zero-external-accounts — 392b6dcf-6e9d-441d-bf7b-64ba362578d7 — as of 2026-10-11

include_smokeshow (default off, full preset) adds a step that uploads the HTML report to an ephemeral public URL with no secret. It runs only on public repositories, last in the coverage job, and is best-effort (continue-on-error).

Reason: Codecov is opt-in and non-blocking, so a self-contained project had no hosted, browsable coverage report; smokeshow gives a public project one without an account. Its tokenless endpoint has low rate limits, so a transient failure must neither fail the job that feeds the required check gate nor abort the authoritative Codecov upload; a private report must never be published.

docs.title: Per-component markers, path-filtered jobs, and one coverage gate per component
docs.text:
Id: 467b6cc3-775b-4e4c-9a8e-b0d1c3d733ac Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-028 (docs/adr/028-per-component-markers-and-path-filtered-ci.md) Revisit when: a component gains a dependency on another component's tree, or the aggregation action changes how it treats skipped jobs See: ci-topology.md#a-single-union-coverage-gate-across-the-whole-matrix — ca90a48d-f648-40b3-ae1a-05f9f21cf411 — as of 2026-10-11 See: architecture-contracts.md#one-exhaustive-import-linter-layers-contract-cli-above-independent-components-above-core-above-utils — 3b7cdbee-7c66-4e52-9d7e-8ab0ffe32e56 — as of 2026-10-11

One pytest marker per enabled component plus core, applied automatically by a root conftest.py hook from each test's top-level tests/<dir>/. A changes path-filter job emits one boolean per component plus core; the monolithic CI job splits into test-core (always) and test-<component> jobs gated on their own filter or core. Each coverage-<component> job merges that component's OS cells and enforces fail_under = 99 scoped to its subtree via --include; coverage-core uses --omit of every component and re-adds */_version.py because a CLI --omit overrides the pyproject one. A non-gating coverage-report job merges what ran, omitting skipped components so their unexecuted files are not reported at zero, and publishes to Codecov, smokeshow and SonarCloud. The check gate lists every path-gated job as an allowed skip. The default tox run is unchanged.

Reason: every component's suite ran on every OS for a one-line change in another component, and a contributor had no knob to run only one component. core is the escape hatch — it watches dependencies, the shared core/ tree, root modules and root tests, so a change underpinning every component forces the full fan-out, mirroring the import layering. Per-component skipping is incompatible with a single union gate, so the gate is decomposed; skipping is sound because an unchanged subtree has nothing to regress. The cross-OS union is kept within a component, where a per-cell gate would wrongly fail on a platform-gated branch. The aggregation action counts a skipped job as a failure unless named, hence the allowed-skips list rendered from the same component list as needs.

Consequence: a full run fans out to more jobs than before; the win is on component-scoped PRs. --include/--omit patterns must match both the editable and installed layouts (*/-anchored) and are verifiable only through a real tox run. Adding a component touches the marker list, the conftest directory set, the filters, two jobs and the omit list in lockstep.

docs.title: Asymmetric matrix: every interpreter on Linux, one representative elsewhere; style and installed-CLI are separate jobs
docs.text:
Id: 4457f652-2a84-4d70-ab7a-e9d1ebd9c670 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-029 (docs/adr/029-asymmetric-ci-matrix-and-draft-pr-skip.md); issue #159 Revisit when: a platform-specific interpreter defect slips through often enough to matter, or a C-extension build no longer differs per OS/interpreter pair See: ci-topology.md#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component — 467b6cc3-775b-4e4c-9a8e-b0d1c3d733ac — as of 2026-10-11

Each test-* job runs Python 3.10 through 3.14 on Ubuntu and the invoking interpreter on macOS and Windows; with include_c_extensions every OS runs all five. style runs once on Ubuntu, with mypy additionally run for the win32 and darwin platforms. With include_cli, a cli-installed job runs the installed console-script check on all three OSes. Explicit tox env lists keep style and CLI execution out of the component jobs.

Reason: cross-platform behaviour needs every OS at one interpreter and interpreter compatibility needs every interpreter on one OS; the full cross-product repeats two mostly independent dimensions. Type checkers prune sys.platform branches against their host, so the platform flags keep static coverage of platform-gated code. Marker arguments forwarded to pytest must not reach the cli tox env, which would call the installed command with pytest's -m option instead of its default argument.

Consequence: a defect needing one particular non-Linux OS and a non-representative interpreter may pass CI — the accepted cost.

docs.title: Every generated CI job skips draft pull requests
docs.text:
Id: 43288d9b-11b3-4d92-8a84-6efe1aa43001 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-029 (docs/adr/029-asymmetric-ci-matrix-and-draft-pr-skip.md) Revisit when: GitHub adds ready_for_review to the default trigger set, or drafts need a cheap smoke run

Every job in ci.yml carries the falsy-safe condition that the pull request is not a draft, composed with existing conditions rather than replacing them (check keeps always(), SonarCloud its fork guard, component jobs their change filters). The pull_request trigger explicitly includes ready_for_review. Security and docs-preview workflows still run on drafts.

Reason: drafts paid for the whole fan-out before review. != true keeps running on push and manual events where the pull-request object is absent, unlike == false. Without ready_for_review, a PR opened as a draft could stay permanently skipped after becoming reviewable. Draft PRs skip check itself, so they need no allowed-skip entry.

docs.title: Runnable components and the console root
Secondary components are subcommands of one console root, not separate scripts
docs.text:
Id: 3d60ab14-8ff9-47db-b326-d7e82947a6cf Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-019 (docs/adr/019-components-as-cli-subcommands.md), including its 2026-09 amendment; issue #203 Revisit when: a new kind of runnable component is added, or typer becomes unacceptable on the minimal launcher See: architecture-contracts.md#one-exhaustive-import-linter-layers-contract-cli-above-independent-components-above-core-above-utils — 3b7cdbee-7c66-4e52-9d7e-8ab0ffe32e56 — as of 2026-10-11 See: components.md#the-web-component-gets-run-and-dev-launch-verbs-and-therefore-always-a-console-root — 3daefc4a-ee36-44cb-b137-bc9224f2a262 — as of 2026-10-11

The highest-precedence enabled component (CLI > GUI > TUI > web > MCP > worker, spelled once as primary_component in copier.yml) owns the bare <pkg> command. Every other enabled component is a lazily imported subcommand (interactive, gui, web, mcp, worker); no <pkg>-<name> console script is emitted. A root exists only where it buys something, captured by the hidden include_console_root: with include_cli, with web, or with two or more components. With no root, bare <pkg> dispatches to the sole component from __main__. GUI uses [project.gui-scripts] only as the sole runnable component; a GUI primary sharing a root gets a normal console script.

Reason: a multi-component project installed four or five sibling executables, a separate script is invisible until you know its name, and the CLI already exposed interactive/gui/web subcommands beside their suffixed scripts while MCP and worker had none. A windowless launcher as the shared root would swallow console I/O and --help of the subcommands on Windows. One computed variable is the single source for the cli/ package, the typer dependency, the import-linter orchestrator layer and the __main__ branch, so typer stays off a single-component non-CLI app.

Rejected alternative: a universal root for every app — forces typer onto single-component non-CLI apps and dilutes what include_cli means.

Rejected alternative: keep suffixed scripts when no CLI is present — leaves the PATH and discoverability problem for non-CLI multi-component apps.

Consequence: the package directory is named cli/ even in a launcher-only project; adopters updating lose the suffixed scripts and switch wrappers to the subcommand form.

docs.title: cli_framework offers argparse beside Typer; the Typer dependency is gated on root_uses_typer
docs.text:
Id: de9f8183-4328-4678-8611-5e715cffd70d Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-020 (docs/adr/020-cli-framework-choice.md); issue #205 Revisit when: demand appears for click as a third choice, or a no-CLI launcher needs to be framework-free See: components.md#secondary-components-are-subcommands-of-one-console-root-not-separate-scripts — 3d60ab14-8ff9-47db-b326-d7e82947a6cf — as of 2026-10-11 See: package-distribution.md#homebrew-and-scoop-are-opt-in-dispatches-the-tap-or-bucket-owns-the-manifest-logic — 462ac46c-c9db-4a4a-b8ae-bbe5c14af09f — as of 2026-10-11

A cli_framework sub-question (typer default, argparse), asked only with include_cli, mirrors web_framework. The argparse root is standard-library only and contract-equivalent: same version/info commands, same lazily imported component subcommands, help on no arguments, non-zero exit on missing metadata. A no-CLI launcher keeps the Typer root. The typer entry in dependencies and the cli/app.py branch both read one hidden root_uses_typer variable.

Reason: include_cli was hardwired to Typer, so a genuine command-line tool that wanted no framework had no supported path to is_app and therefore none to Homebrew/Scoop packaging; forcing toggles via --data did not persist. The dependency is gated on root_uses_typer rather than on the framework answer because Copier retains unasked answers: a project that set argparse, then turned the CLI off while keeping two components, carries the stored answer forward while rendering the Typer root — a launcher importing typer without declaring it, broken even in a synced environment. An earlier revision of the record claimed the simpler guard was correct in every case; it was not.

Rejected alternative: widen the is_app gate for libraries — a framework-free CLI is made a first-class way to be an app instead.

Rejected alternative: click as a third choice — a dependency without Typer's ergonomics; earns its keep only on later demand.

docs.title: Launcher imports are guarded with exact-match, preflighted dependency errors
docs.text:
Id: 70e54068-d43c-40a2-9097-95e7cc14c668 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-028 (docs/adr/028-actionable-component-dependency-guard.md); issues #172 and #268 Revisit when: generated projects gain per-component extras, or a dependency stops importing lazily after the guarded block See: components.md#secondary-components-are-subcommands-of-one-console-root-not-separate-scripts — 3d60ab14-8ff9-47db-b326-d7e82947a6cf — as of 2026-10-11 See: components.md#component-dependencies-are-core-dependencies-there-is-no-empty-all-extra — e9b25624-f621-4071-bd99-a7cde620189a — as of 2026-10-11

Each launcher's lazy import is wrapped in a context manager that turns a ModuleNotFoundError whose name is exactly one of the component's declared dependency modules into an exit-1 message naming the component, the module and the fix (uv sync). Dependencies that import late (uvicorn, Tkinter, textual) or re-export behind their own guard with no module name (faststream brokers, mcp's transitive imports) are imported eagerly inside the block by a preflight that re-raises with the caller-supplied name. Tkinter gets a system-package hint (including a version-qualified Homebrew formula) because it is not a distribution. The root's own module-scope imports (typer, pydantic via the settings stack) and the sole-component entrypoint in __main__.py get the same treatment; all derived facts are when: false computed variables in copier.yml.

Reason: there are no extras to name — component deps are core dependencies — so a missing module means the environment is out of sync with the metadata and uv sync is the honest remedy. The first-party import always succeeds after a copier update; the third-party failure happens one frame deeper, so the guard must classify what comes out of the import rather than replace it. Exact matching protects application defects (a typo'd import below an installed dependency) from being mislabelled as a stale environment. The sole-component entrypoint is what frozen binaries target, whose user has no CLI to fall back on. Shared computed variables matter most for the two guards rendered into different files, only one of which exists in any project.

Rejected alternative: a shared require(module, feature, extra) helper as the issue proposed — no extra exists, and replacing the first-party import would not catch the deeper failure.

Rejected alternative: guard every component's module scope so direct library imports also get the message — the reader is already in a traceback in their own code, the guard would run on every successful import forever, and component modules are what adopters edit most.

Rejected alternative: let faststream's own ImportError through — its advice (pip install "faststream[<broker>]") bypasses the lockfile.

docs.title: Component dependencies are core dependencies; there is no empty all extra
docs.text:
Id: e9b25624-f621-4071-bd99-a7cde620189a Type: decision Type: constraint Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-028 (docs/adr/028-no-empty-all-extra.md) Revisit when: a component gains a genuinely optional dependency

Generated projects declare no [project.optional-dependencies] table. A runnable component's runtime dependency goes into the core dependencies list under its toggle guard. The permanently empty all = [], the <pkg>[all] dev self-reference, six extras = ["all"] tox settings and four --extra all workflow flags were removed.

Reason: a component is chosen at generation time and __main__ imports it unconditionally, so a plain install must pull its dependency or the console script fails at launch. The leftover shell installed nothing yet three documents cited it as load-bearing — a reader auditing the packaging would have concluded the wrong thing about what guarantees what.

Rejected alternative: keep all = [] as a pre-wired seam for a future optional dependency — a one-time edit if ever needed is cheaper than a permanent misleading declaration.

Consequence: adopters applying this update must re-lock, because the metadata recorded in uv.lock changes and every uv run --locked hard-fails until they do; a hand-added uv run --extra all breaks.

docs.title: The web component gets run and dev launch verbs, and therefore always a console root
docs.text:
Id: 3daefc4a-ee36-44cb-b137-bc9224f2a262 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-032 (docs/adr/032-uniform-run-dev-launch-verbs.md); issue #177 Revisit when: FastStream's reload stops requiring its CLI extra, or a second component acquires a prod/dev distinction See: components.md#secondary-components-are-subcommands-of-one-console-root-not-separate-scripts — 3d60ab14-8ff9-47db-b326-d7e82947a6cf — as of 2026-10-11 See: components.md#launcher-imports-are-guarded-with-exact-match-preflighted-dependency-errors — 70e54068-d43c-40a2-9097-95e7cc14c668 — as of 2026-10-11

<pkg> run [module:attribute] starts the web app on the configured bind; <pkg> dev adds autoreload and forces a loopback bind. Both share one private runner and the dependency guard; <pkg> web stays as an alias where web is not primary. The target is passed to uvicorn as an import string, validated for shape only — no module search, no framework sniffing. include_console_root now includes include_web, so a web-only project reaches its component through the minimal launcher.

Reason: varying the app object or reload meant dropping to a different framework CLI per framework that the project's own help never mentioned. uvicorn is already a web runtime dependency and takes an import string with reload natively; the string form is the only one that can reload in a child process, so one code path serves both modes. A reloading server executes unreviewed code on every save and belongs on loopback. A web-only project had no root to hang a verb on, and standalone <pkg>-run/<pkg>-dev scripts are the second entry scheme the subcommand decision exists to prevent.

Rejected alternative: verbs for the worker too — reload needs faststream[cli] at runtime, which the template deliberately keeps out of dependencies, and type-sniffing the target is the framework detection avoided here.

Rejected alternative: replace <pkg> web with <pkg> run — breaks the one naming rule the subcommand decision makes.

Rejected alternative: let uvicorn parse the target — its error names no project command and is not testable the way a cheap shape check is.

Consequence: web-only Litestar projects gain typer (FastAPI already ships it); sole_component can never be web, so a web project's executable entrypoint is the console root.

docs.title: One application payload in core/app.py; components are adapters over it
docs.text:
Id: 8bb1e55e-f468-44fc-80a5-d3b3719e5ddc Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-033 (docs/adr/033-shared-app-service-components-as-adapters.md); issues #178 and #321 Revisit when: a component needs a fourth failure behaviour, or a second provider of the payload appears See: architecture-contracts.md#one-exhaustive-import-linter-layers-contract-cli-above-independent-components-above-core-above-utils — 3b7cdbee-7c66-4e52-9d7e-8ab0ffe32e56 — as of 2026-10-11 See: template-updates.md#retired-template-modules-become-adopter-owned — 4dd6729a-697e-4588-a7a7-d37152018b6b — as of 2026-10-11

core/app.py exposes three functions — version() and info(), which raise MetadataUnavailableError, and info_or_unknown(), which degrades, logs and never raises — plus the error type and an unknown-version constant. Each component imports the module as service and adapts: the CLI exits 1, the web app answers 503, the MCP tool returns error text, GUI and TUI show "unknown", the worker falls back to 0.0.0. The module renders only when a runnable component is enabled. One missing_metadata fixture patching core.app.Distribution replaces six per-module stubs.

Reason: a full project carried eight copies of the distribution lookup and six of the platform payload, with nothing enforcing agreement — GUI and TUI nearly drifted on field names and fatality. The import contract forbids components importing each other, so sharing had to live below them, and core is already that layer. Functions rather than a class because it would hold no state and ruff's no-self-use rule flags exactly that shape; no Protocol because it would have one implementation and no type-checking caller. Three functions because there are three real behaviours, each with more than one caller. Logging stays in the adapters because it genuinely differs; the worker's wire model keeps its own platform fields because routing them through a dict adds indirection for no sharing.

Rejected alternative: a new base/ package with an AppService class and a VersionProvider protocol, as proposed — each adds a name without adding a constraint.

Rejected alternative: a transport/presentation split per component — more files than the three f-strings they would hold.

Rejected alternative: keep the copies and add a conformance test — tells you they drifted after the sixth copy is written; removing them means they cannot.

docs.title: Sphinx with the bare Shibuya theme replaces MkDocs
docs.text:
Id: 5133caa8-3231-4d4d-877b-041b315cb87a Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-006 (docs/adr/006-sphinx-shibuya-for-documentation.md) Revisit when: Shibuya stops being published on PyPI, or the Litestar-org reference sites change stack

Generated projects document with Sphinx, the shibuya theme from PyPI, reStructuredText sources (MyST enabled for Markdown pages), autodoc plus napoleon for the API reference, and a set of extensions matching the Litestar organization's sites. Docs builds install the package, not only the docs group. Publishing still goes through the gh-pages branch, so no Pages setting changed.

Reason: the MkDocs 2.0 line was unstable and pinning 1.x indefinitely was a dead end; the shipped MkDocs setup installed mkdocs-material without configuring it and hand-maintained an API page that did not track the code. The visual target (Litestar, Advanced Alchemy, Polyfactory) turned out to be Sphinx plus Shibuya, so adopting that stack is the direct path. Autodoc must import the package and the modules' dependencies, hence the package install.

Rejected alternative: litestar-sphinx-theme — Shibuya plus Litestar branding, distributed as a git dependency; wrong for a generic template.

Rejected alternative: sphinxcontrib-typer for the CLI reference — works, but generating the page from the live app at build time keeps the CLI uniform with the worker and web generators and adds no extension; sphinx-click is unusable because Typer vendors its own Click.

Consequence: the --unsafe YAML-check flag that existed only for mkdocs.yml was dropped; conf.py gets a ruff per-file ignore; a duplicate docstring autodoc surfaced and was removed.

docs.title: PR docs previews deploy to a subfolder of the project's own gh-pages, same-repo only
docs.text:
Id: 55a74975-a6e0-4f18-8254-fa27f047e829 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-010 §1 (docs/adr/010-pr-docs-previews-and-released-issue-notifications.md) Revisit when: the preview action ships fork support, or previews need to block merges See: external-integrations.md#a-freshly-generated-project-is-green-on-first-push-with-zero-external-accounts — 392b6dcf-6e9d-441d-bf7b-64ba362578d7 — as of 2026-10-11 See: docs-versioning.md#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages — 858025c1-19a6-46f6-a237-01ba6477262a — as of 2026-10-11

A single-job docs-preview.yml on pull_request builds the Sphinx HTML and hands deploy, removal on close and a sticky comment to a purpose-built action, publishing under pr-preview/pr-<N>/ on the project's own gh-pages. It runs only when the head repository is the repository itself; fork PRs skip cleanly. It renders only when include_docs is on (ADR-025) and is not in the check gate.

Reason: the upstream pattern deployed to a separate repository with a GitHub App token — a second repo and App to provision. Same-repo pull_request carries a write token and needs no dangerous-triggers ignore because untrusted fork code never runs with write access; for a solo-maintainer template, same-repo branches are the common case. Removing a subfolder on close and maintaining a comment would otherwise mean hand-rolled git on gh-pages, exactly the surface the released-docs deploy moved away from. A bare artifact has no live URL, which is the whole value.

Rejected alternative: a workflow_run/pull_request_target split for fork coverage — deferred until the action supports forks.

Consequence: the released-docs deploys exclude pr-preview/** from cleaning and merge rather than force-push, so previews survive a release and a racing deploy cannot overwrite them.

docs.title: sphinx-lint and the case-conflict hook are always-on; link checking is weekly
docs.text:
Id: 726d9de8-c1d3-4974-9019-76c8bb5ffc5b Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-011 (docs/adr/011-docs-linting-and-cross-platform-filename-safety.md) Revisit when: the matrix drops a case-insensitive platform, or linkcheck becomes reliable enough for PR time See: ci-topology.md#network-dependent-checks-run-on-a-weekly-cron-never-in-the-merge-gate — 3e5b9525-9087-4125-b19f-80f6c226c01f — as of 2026-10-11 See: architecture-contracts.md#whole-program-analyzers-are-local-system-hooks-backed-by-the-style-group — 41f3397d-1afb-4e57-a0bd-b5ef85089bfc — as of 2026-10-11

sphinx-lint runs in the tox style env and as a prek local hook from the same style group pin, scoped to .rst files. check-case-conflict is a prek builtin, not a style tool. A docs-linkcheck tox env runs Sphinx's linkcheck, driven by a weekly scheduled workflow and manual dispatch, never on pull requests and never in check.

Reason: nothing checked the RST sources for markup Sphinx tolerates silently, nothing caught link rot, and nothing caught two filenames differing only in case — fine on Linux, a collision on the Windows and macOS matrix cells. All three are account-free, so always-on fits. Link checking hits the network and is inherently flaky; a dead external link must never block an unrelated merge.

docs.title: Sphinx warnings use an exact, reviewable allowlist
docs.text:
Id: 2a555902-38e7-47d4-a231-445a8e6caa0f Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: issue #187, PR #242; commit ab6a857; docs/template-architecture.md, Sphinx warning gate Verification: corroborated — the rendered warning checker compares normalized sets in both directions, and the docs-build environment invokes it Revisit when: Sphinx changes warning formatting or a previously unavoidable warning disappears See: docs-versioning.md#the-sphinx-warning-gate-runs-in-a-job-the-required-check-context-aggregates — bc382803-5aa9-4582-9bad-1c9efef8fc49 — as of 2026-10-11

The docs-build gate captures Sphinx warnings and compares them with a committed allowlist. It rejects both new unexpected warnings and expected warnings that are no longer emitted. The default allowlist is empty. Normalization removes machine-specific path prefixes and folds Windows separators, while preserving line numbers. Sphinx's nitpicky mode remains off.

Reason: an individually justified upstream warning should not force a choice between permanently red documentation builds and broad warning suppression. Exact entries make exceptions reviewable; the reverse comparison prevents obsolete exceptions from accumulating silently.

Rejected alternative: make every warning fatal directly through Sphinx's warning-as-error mode. It was superseded by the allowlist so unavoidable exceptions can coexist with a regression gate.

Alternative deferred: enable nitpicky immediately. The issue anticipated a noisy initial cross-reference cleanup and left this for a separate pass. Removing line numbers was also considered but not selected; no further reason for that choice was established in the reviewed sources.

docs.title: The Sphinx subsystem is toggleable (include_docs, default on); the maintainer guide is not
docs.text:
Id: e983d1e7-421f-4926-9415-a3da4626f220 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-025 (docs/adr/025-optional-docs-subsystem.md); issue #252 Revisit when: the six files that hard-reference docs/maintaining/setup.rst move, or a preset wants docs off by default See: repo-setup.md#maintainer-repository-setup-has-one-actor-tagged-home-in-the-docs-tree — 4e0fcdab-d3b9-4f96-b61d-8e34927af98d — as of 2026-10-11

One boolean gates the whole Sphinx site: the docs/ pages, the docs dependency group, the docs-* tox envs, sphinx-lint in style and prek, the docs workflows, the deploy-docs release job and the related README, support and contributing links. It defaults on in every preset. docs/maintaining/ ships regardless; only its GitHub Pages step is conditional.

Reason: docs was the only substantial subsystem with no toggle, and a small library or internal tool often wants a README and nothing more. Default-on keeps copier update non-breaking and the published-site baseline. The maintainer setup guide is read as plain text by the repo-setup skill and hard-referenced from six other files, so relocating it would break all of them; a docs/ directory holding just the guide is preferable.

Consequence: a README-only project is a supported shape; the later docs-dependent features (tested examples, CLI reference, versioned docs) are gated by construction.

docs.title: Documentation code examples are executed, not pasted
docs.text:
Id: 2a95e867-8cca-44e9-9844-a7109e5f6a7b Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-028 (docs/adr/028-tested-documentation-examples.md) Revisit when: another Markdown file is adopted as a doctest surface, or the per-component CI jobs stop replacing tox's default env list See: docs-stack.md#the-sphinx-subsystem-is-toggleable-include_docs-default-on-the-maintainer-guide-is-not — e983d1e7-421f-4926-9415-a3da4626f220 — as of 2026-10-11

Complete Python examples live in docs/examples/, rendered into Sphinx pages with literalinclude and imported or called by the regular pytest suite. The directory is in scope for ruff, every type checker and pylint, but outside the package and coverage source set. The Sphinx doctest extension runs inline >>> snippets through a docs-doctest tox env and a dedicated CI job in the check gate. The top-level README.md is a pytest testpaths entry collected with a doctest glob for that basename only; tests/conftest.py ignores *.md so no future tests/**/README.md is swept in, and the prek pytest hook runs bare pytest so testpaths is honoured. README examples leave a blank line before the closing fence because doctest ends expected output at the first blank line.

Reason: pasted fences drift silently from the API; neither the suite nor the static gates execute them, which the template's high coverage bar otherwise makes easy to miss. The dedicated doctest job exists because the per-component test jobs pass marker arguments that replace tox's default env list, so doctests would never run otherwise. Examples are documentation, not product code, hence outside coverage.

Rejected alternative: an explicit pytest tests target in the hook — would let a broken README doctest pass locally and surface only in CI.

Consequence: the Sphinx builder owns .rst prose and pytest owns the one curated Markdown surface; neither collector overlaps the other.

docs.title: The four auto-generated reference pages keep their current generators
docs.text:
Id: aa157658-027b-42c3-8a2b-1e6b40b6b739 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-038 (docs/adr/038-sphinx-api-reference-rendering-strategy.md), refreshed 2026-10-05 Revisit when: a sphinxcontrib-openapi pilot confirms OpenAPI 3.1 rendering, an AsyncAPI Sphinx renderer appears, or argparse CLIs are judged to need a reference page See: docs-stack.md#sphinx-with-the-bare-shibuya-theme-replaces-mkdocs — 5133caa8-3231-4d4d-877b-041b315cb87a — as of 2026-10-11

The CLI (Typer), config (autodoc-pydantic), OpenAPI and AsyncAPI references are all derived from the live app at build time, nothing committed. The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI pages are raw spec dumps via literalinclude; none of the surveyed extensions is adopted now. sphinxcontrib-openapi is the designated future upgrade for OpenAPI; sphinx-argparse-cli the candidate if argparse CLIs get a page; an AsyncAPI renderer does not exist and would be an upstream contribution.

Reason: every extension is another docs dependency to pin, so the bar is a rendering upgrade large enough to justify it — met only for OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, where today's output is a dump. Native-rST rendering is the only style consistent with the offline, self-contained docs posture; ReDoc, Swagger-UI (CDN by default), RapiDoc and the embeddable bundles ship a JS app into the docs. sphinxcontrib-typer covers only Typer, so argparse would still need separate handling. asyncapi-sphinx-ext is early-stage, stale, and wants channels authored in docstrings rather than consuming a generated spec.

Rejected alternative: sphinx-pydantic — abandoned. pydantic-kitbash and sphinx-jsonschema — no advantage for a settings reference.

Consequence: sphinxcontrib-openapi's OpenAPI 3.1 support has lagged and both frameworks emit 3.1, so a pilot must precede adoption.

docs.title: Docs publish only the current version and carry older built versions forward from gh-pages
docs.text:
Id: 858025c1-19a6-46f6-a237-01ba6477262a Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-027 §1–2 (docs/adr/027-versioned-documentation-and-last-updated-stamps.md); issue #165; the Litestar docs build is the model Revisit when: a Sphinx multiversion tool stops rebuilding old tags, or conf.py stops running build-time generators against the live app See: docs-stack.md#sphinx-with-the-bare-shibuya-theme-replaces-mkdocs — 5133caa8-3231-4d4d-877b-041b315cb87a — as of 2026-10-11 See: docs-stack.md#pr-docs-previews-deploy-to-a-subfolder-of-the-projects-own-gh-pages-same-repo-only — 55a74975-a6e0-4f18-8254-fa27f047e829 — as of 2026-10-11

A generated tools/build_docs.py computes the version slug, enumerates the version directories already on gh-pages, writes a generated (gitignored) versions.json for Shibuya's native switcher, builds only the current ref, copies every other version directory across from gh-pages, writes a root redirect to latest (the highest non-prerelease by PEP 440 ordering), and deploys with previews excluded from cleaning. Versioned publishing is how a docs-enabled project always publishes; it is not a toggle. The version list is stateless: gh-pages is the source of truth, and local builds hide the switcher because no versions.json exists.

Reason: sphinx-multiversion (effectively unmaintained) and sphinx-polyversion both rebuild every selected tag on every deploy. This template's conf.py runs subprocess generators against the live app, so rebuilding a historical tag re-runs that tag's generators against whatever the build resolves — fragile, slow, and it forces every past conf.py to keep building forever. Litestar's build-current-preserve-rest model avoids that. Litestar commits and hand-edits its version list, which is untenable with per-minor granularity and automated releases, and having CI commit back to a protected main adds real machinery.

Rejected alternative: sphinx-multiversion or sphinx-polyversion — the rebuild model above.

Rejected alternative: a committed versions.json — the hand-edit or CI-commit cost above.

Consequence: gh-pages becomes load-bearing state; both deploy paths must preserve the numeric version-slug directories. An older version's switcher is frozen at its build time, so the switcher appears only from the first versioned release onward.

docs.title: Version granularity is a scaffold-time question
docs.text:
Id: 5d18c9af-73e9-476b-9ba9-544c776812e6 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-027 §3 (docs/adr/027-versioned-documentation-and-last-updated-stamps.md) Revisit when: the pre-1.0 minor-is-breaking bump policy changes See: docs-versioning.md#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages — 858025c1-19a6-46f6-a237-01ba6477262a — as of 2026-10-11 See: release-automation.md#release-please-is-the-sole-release-orchestrator — 7ec8a937-fd4d-41f2-96b7-824fe3be913b — as of 2026-10-11

docs_version_granularity (asked with include_docs) offers minor (X.Y, default), major (X) and full (X.Y.Z). The choice bakes a slicing constant into the generated build script, overridable at build time only by the manual redeploy.

Reason: granularity is the one knob adopters reasonably differ on. minor matches the pre-1.0 posture where minors are the breaking bump; a large project picks major, an archival one full. Prerelease slugs survive only under full and are excluded from latest.

docs.title: The manual redeploy rebuilds the latest published release, never HEAD
docs.text:
Id: f0ad70ba-c790-42d2-94f0-152e9527be4f Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-027 §4 (docs/adr/027-versioned-documentation-and-last-updated-stamps.md) Revisit when: release-please stops creating the tag before the release is published, or the build script's granularity stops being baked in See: docs-versioning.md#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages — 858025c1-19a6-46f6-a237-01ba6477262a — as of 2026-10-11 See: release-automation.md#the-release-is-created-as-a-draft-finalized-after-artifacts-attach — 398b3cd9-e57b-4856-b2c7-76752c0ec37f — as of 2026-10-11

gh-pages.yml (manual dispatch only) routes through the build script, checks out the tag of the latest published release via the releases API, sets up the interpreter after that checkout, restores the build script itself from the dispatch ref, and passes the tag's baked granularity back through the environment.

Reason: a naive root publish would wipe every version directory. The tag comes from the API rather than git describe because release-please creates the tag the moment the release PR merges and leaves the release a draft until publishing succeeds — so git describe would pick an unreleased version in exactly the window a redeploy is most likely (right after a failed release). The interpreter setup follows the checkout so the tagged docs build on the Python the release shipped on. The script is orchestration, same layer as the workflow, and an older tagged copy could carry the version-dropping bug the loud-fetch rule prevents; its granularity is not orchestration — which slug a release occupies is fixed at publish time — so an adopter who changed the answer later must not republish a tag under a second slug and repoint latest.

Rejected alternative: git describe --tags — selects draft tags.

Rejected alternative: use the dispatch revision's granularity — duplicates a released version under a new slug.

docs.title: A failed gh-pages fetch must abort, never fall through as "branch absent"
docs.text:
Id: 135cfbb5-6c5c-45d8-9239-cf225a819818 Type: decision Type: incident Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-027 §4a (docs/adr/027-versioned-documentation-and-last-updated-stamps.md) Revisit when: the deploy stops cleaning the target, or git fetch learns to distinguish a missing ref from a transport error See: docs-versioning.md#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages — 858025c1-19a6-46f6-a237-01ba6477262a — as of 2026-10-11

Both deploy paths probe the branch with git ls-remote --exit-code and branch on its exit code: 2 means no such ref, anything else aborts. One layer up, the build script's preserve step raises when a version subtree it was handed cannot be read; only the latest alias is optional.

Reason: the previous fetch || echo swallowed every failure, not only a missing ref. The build script then assembled a site with no prior versions and the clean deploy deleted every published version directory — one transient transport error destroys the documentation archive for every prior release. Every slug the preserve step receives came from a listing of that very ref, so it provably exists and silently omitting it is the same deletion by another route.

docs.title: Per-page "last updated" comes from git history
docs.text:
Id: 7e34868f-a26a-4c89-8189-f5778ad9a04b Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-027 §5 (docs/adr/027-versioned-documentation-and-last-updated-stamps.md) Revisit when: a docs job checks out with shallow history See: docs-stack.md#sphinx-warnings-use-an-exact-reviewable-allowlist — 2a555902-38e7-47d4-a231-445a8e6caa0f — as of 2026-10-11

sphinx-last-updated-by-git is in the docs group; every page footer shows the commit date of its source. Any untracked-source warning from the generated fragments goes through the warning allowlist, not blanket suppression.

Reason: readers could not tell how fresh a page was; git history is a cheap offline freshness signal.

Consequence: every docs build needs full history (fetch-depth: 0), including the CI job that runs the warning gate.

docs.title: The Sphinx warning gate runs in a job the required check context aggregates
docs.text:
Id: bc382803-5aa9-4582-9bad-1c9efef8fc49 Type: decision Type: incident Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-027, Consequences (docs/adr/027-versioned-documentation-and-last-updated-stamps.md) Revisit when: docs-doctest is renamed or leaves the check aggregation See: docs-stack.md#sphinx-warnings-use-an-exact-reviewable-allowlist — 2a555902-38e7-47d4-a231-445a8e6caa0f — as of 2026-10-11 See: ci-topology.md#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component — 467b6cc3-775b-4e4c-9a8e-b0d1c3d733ac — as of 2026-10-11

tox -e docs-build (Sphinx with warnings captured plus the allowlist checker) runs in ci.yml's docs-doctest job, which check aggregates.

Reason: it previously ran only in the docs-preview workflow, which forks skip and no protected branch requires, so a PR introducing broken references kept every required context green. The doctest job on its own runs the doctest builder with no warnings-as-errors and no allowlist, so it never covered this. A gate must be checked by which context a protected branch sees, not by whether the job runs.

docs.title: External integrations and the self-contained default
A freshly generated project is green on first push with zero external accounts
docs.text:
Id: 392b6dcf-6e9d-441d-bf7b-64ba362578d7 Type: constraint Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-009, ADR-010, ADR-011, ADR-013, ADR-017, ADR-018, ADR-021, ADR-026, ADR-034 (docs/adr/) Revisit when: the template's target audience shifts to teams that provision external services as a matter of course

The template's default posture: anything that needs an external service, a secret, a personal access token or a per-owner repository is an opt-in toggle defaulting to false; anything self-contained and zero-config may be always-on. Secret-gated jobs skip with a visible notice or warning instead of failing, and such jobs never join the check merge gate unless the project owner requires them through branch protection.

Reason: an integration forced on without its setup is inert or noisy — a SonarCloud job with no token fails, an unmaintained contributors grid rots, a multi-gigabyte linter image slows every push — and most of them duplicate gates the template already ships. Keeping the default fast and account-free is what lets a scaffold be green on its first push. This is the shared rationale the per-integration entries cite rather than restate.

Rejected alternative: ship the integrations always-on because mature projects use them. Rejected for the failure modes above.

docs.title: Sourcery, SonarCloud and all-contributors are independent opt-in toggles
docs.text:
Id: e926a0ce-c030-4a76-8b11-41c450bb43f4 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-009 (docs/adr/009-optional-external-quality-community-integrations.md), including its 2026-07 amendment Revisit when: one of the three services gains a provisioning-free mode, or a fourth integration of the same shape is proposed See: external-integrations.md#a-freshly-generated-project-is-green-on-first-push-with-zero-external-accounts — 392b6dcf-6e9d-441d-bf7b-64ba362578d7 — as of 2026-10-11 See: standalone-executables.md#three-architecture-named-executable-toggles-instead-of-one-brand-toggle — d5aed1a0-0b7c-4ac3-9d75-fb9568d9e34d — as of 2026-10-11

include_sourcery renders only a config file (the GitHub App does the work; no workflow surface). include_sonarcloud adds a sonar CI job that runs only on same-repo events and records a visible skip when SONAR_TOKEN is unset. include_all_contributors renders the config, a README section and a small workflow that runs the all-contributors CLI (delivered through mise's npm backend, Renovate-tracked) and opens a pull request with the regenerated table — it never pushes to the default branch, so the toggle is useful without the bot.

Reason: all three depend on out-of-band provisioning and overlap with tooling already shipped (SonarCloud with Codecov, CodeQL, ruff and the type checkers; Sourcery with ruff's refactor rules). Teams that already run them get a correctly wired start instead of hand-rolling config. The amendment gave all-contributors a first-party path so the toggle no longer depends solely on an external bot.

Rejected alternative: always-on — breaks the self-contained default.

Rejected alternative: omit them entirely — loses the first-class starting point and the discoverability of the option.

Rejected alternative: one shared enum or parent toggle — they solve different problems and compose freely, mirroring the independent-boolean precedent of the executable toggles.

Consequence: the all-contributors workflow needs the repository setting that lets Actions create pull requests, which release-please already requires.

docs.title: Opt-in benchmarking with pytest-codspeed
docs.text:
Id: 841ba12d-3ad2-402e-9c7e-6791b8221952 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-034 (docs/adr/034-opt-in-performance-benchmarking.md) Revisit when: a benchmarking service becomes usable without an account, or the default CI budget changes See: external-integrations.md#a-freshly-generated-project-is-green-on-first-push-with-zero-external-accounts — 392b6dcf-6e9d-441d-bf7b-64ba362578d7 — as of 2026-10-11

include_benchmarks (default off, on in the full preset) renders a benchmarks/ starter suite, a benchmark pytest marker excluded from the ordinary run, benchmark tox/mise entry points and a separate benchmarks.yml workflow. The workflow is gated on CODSPEED_TOKEN, emits a notice when it is not configured, and stays out of the check gate.

Reason: correctness and coverage gates do not catch a valid change that makes a hot path materially slower, but timings must not slow every project's default CI or require an account. Service setup is an explicit, reversible owner choice.

Alternatives: unknown — ADR-034 records the decision and its constraints, no alternative that was in contention.

docs.title: cobo generates the gitignore with a hash-sealed fence and lockfiles
docs.text:
Id: 3e3bc38e-bc1e-4e65-b74d-e91848262157 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-012 (docs/adr/012-cobo-for-gitignore-generation.md) Revisit when: github/gitignore stops being the boilerplate source, or cobo changes its fence or lock format See: ci-topology.md#network-dependent-checks-run-on-a-weekly-cron-never-in-the-merge-gate — 3e5b9525-9087-4125-b19f-80f6c226c01f — as of 2026-10-11

cobo fetches the same github/gitignore boilerplates the previous gibo workflow stacked, but writes them inside a sha256-sealed fence and records the upstream commit and per-file blobs in cobo.lock. The repository root lock carries two fragments — the template source and this repository's own .gitignore (dogfooding) — and template/cobo.lock ships verbatim so a generated project's gitignore is drift-checkable. cobo is always-included tooling (a mise pipx: tool, Renovate-tracked), with no toggle. The project's own overrides (the freezer spec negation, the C-extension ignore) sit below the end fence, where cobo preserves them; the negation still lands after the fenced *.spec ignore, so it wins.

Reason: gibo was run by hand with no lockfile, no pin the tooling understood and no way to detect upstream drift, and the overrides were injected inside the boilerplate it generated.

Rejected alternative: keep gibo — the gaps above.

Consequence: the cobo-managed .gitignore is excluded from the trailing-whitespace hook, because upstream ships trailing whitespace on some comment lines and trimming inside the fence breaks the seal; cobo.lock is linguist-generated and carries its own 2-space EditorConfig stanza (taplo's *.toml glob does not cover .lock). Regeneration is cobo update followed by cobo sync; a hand edit inside the fence breaks the sha256.

docs.title: The fence is LF-sealed, which corrupts two macOS character-class patterns
docs.text:
Id: a5df0a9c-aa53-4a8c-add6-566326352a0e Type: decision Type: workaround Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-012 §1 (docs/adr/012-cobo-for-gitignore-generation.md); cobo#120/#121 (the upstreamed --eol lf policy), cobo#124, issue #111 Revisit when: cobo#124 ships (normalize terminators only, not a mid-line CR) and the Copier render preserves a lone carriage return in this file

The fence is sealed with cobo's --eol lf policy, persisted as eol = "lf" on the lock fragment. The macOS boilerplate encodes two filenames that end in a carriage return (Icon␍, .HFS+ Private Directory Data␍) as single-line character classes; LF normalization splits each into an unterminated Icon[ (matches nothing, inert) and an orphan ] (ignores a file literally named ]). Those two patterns are knowingly broken in every generated project.

Reason: the template enforces LF everywhere (.gitattributes, EditorConfig, ruff), editorconfig-checker fails on an embedded CR, and — decisively — Copier renders .gitignore.jinja through Jinja, whose lexer normalizes a lone \r to \n at scaffold time. A byte-exact (preserve) seal would therefore report locally modified forever in every generated project. There is no LF-only pattern that matches Icon␍ precisely (Icon? over-matches), so fidelity genuinely requires the CR, and the CR cannot survive the render. These are legacy HFS resource-fork artifacts modern macOS rarely creates and almost never commits — an accepted tradeoff, not "harmless".

Rejected alternative: seal byte-exact and keep the CR — fights the LF invariant and is re-corrupted by the render anyway.

Consequence: the cobo-level fix is necessary but not sufficient; restoring the patterns additionally needs a render that preserves the CR (a raw wrap or a Copier newline carve-out scoped to this file).

docs.title: The tox style env is the sole authoritative lint suite; prek is a fast gate, not a second suite
docs.text:
Id: 9b74fc8b-a808-4f2b-bdbd-9e4253c1b35a Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-003 (docs/adr/003-tox-as-canonical-lint-runner.md), including its 2026-06 update Revisit when: a second orchestrator is proposed, or tool versions gain a second pinning location

Tool versions live in the uv-managed style dependency group and the tox style env runs the full lint/type-check suite from it. Git hooks are always included (the include_precommit toggle was removed) and run via prek as a fast local and CI gate; Renovate keeps both the prek rev pins and the style group current. Pants and Trunk, once default-on orchestrators of the same linters, were first demoted to opt-ins and later removed entirely.

Reason: a default project shipped three orchestrators (tox, Pants, Trunk) pinning ruff, mypy, actionlint and others in three places with three update mechanisms, and the pins had already drifted — a contributor could pass the local suite and fail CI on a rule that changed between two pinned versions. One source of truth makes drift impossible, keeps linting on the uv/tox spine the generated project already uses, and leaves one updater. The prek overlap is deliberate: fast feedback while editing, authoritative coverage in tox; the cost is duplicate execution and at most a brief window between two Renovate PRs, not sustained drift.

Rejected alternative: keep Pants and Trunk as opt-ins — the intermediate state this ADR first established; its 2026-06 update dropped them outright so that the tox style env is the sole orchestrator and nothing can drift against it.

Consequence: MegaLinter, when enabled, is scoped so it cannot drift against the Python toolchain (see its own entry below).

docs.title: Taplo checks do not fetch schemas from generated TOML directives
docs.text:
Id: 152edfc1-817e-4265-ac23-53d2a730cd5f Type: workaround Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: issue #337, PR #338; commit 9e86cb8 Verification: corroborated — generated root TOML omits schema directives while the style environment retains Taplo syntax and formatting checks Revisit when: Taplo provides a verified way to retain editor directives without fetching their schemas during checks See: lint-orchestration.md#semgrep-runs-in-the-style-env-against-a-named-registry-ruleset-never-vendored — 5068081c-24ce-4c39-9cdf-13e0a7c229b4 — as of 2026-10-11

Generated root TOML no longer carries the remote schema directive. Editors can use SchemaStore's filename mapping, while Taplo still checks syntax and canonical formatting without that schema fetch.

Reason: a transient remote schema failure could fail the required style gate on unchanged source. The investigation found that Taplo 0.9.3 still fetched an explicit directive's URL with its no-schema flag, so the apparent offline switch did not solve this failure mode.

Rejected alternative: retain the directive and rely on the no-schema flag. It was tested and rejected because the fetch still occurred. Vendoring a schema was discussed with a maintenance cost, but the reviewed sources do not establish an explicit verdict on that alternative.

This constraint applies to the Taplo pass, not to every style tool: the semgrep entry below separately accepts a registry dependency.

docs.title: The prek gate runs at commit; push-only hooks opt in per hook
docs.text:
Id: 8fd817b4-fab6-4ce1-b80d-59a2ea93016f Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: found while adopting the template in openapipages; reproduced with prek 0.5.5; recorded in ADR-003 (docs/adr/003-tox-as-canonical-lint-runner.md) Verification: corroborated — a hook with no stages ran on pre-commit, pre-push, commit-msg and manual when default_stages was unset Revisit when: a hook other than commitizen-branch needs to run on push

default_stages is ["pre-commit"]. Hooks that belong on push, such as commitizen-branch, declare stages themselves.

Reason: ["pre-commit", "pre-push"] ran every hook without its own stages twice per change, including the whole-project type checkers and pylint, and the push run added no coverage the commit run lacked.

Rejected alternative: dropping default_stages. prek then treats every stage as the default, so file hooks also run on commit-msg.

docs.title: Five type checkers; strict basedpyright replaces pyright
docs.text:
Id: 7e130850-494b-427c-a892-a6b3479dd047 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-005 (docs/adr/005-five-type-checkers-basedpyright-strict.md) Revisit when: ty churn becomes a burden, or two checkers stop catching anything the others miss

The style env invokes mypy (two Python versions), basedpyright at its full strict ruleset, ty, pyrefly and zuban. pyright is dropped from the group and the env. Generated code is fixed to satisfy strict rules rather than relaxing the checker; the only suppressions are localized # pyright: ignore comments at genuine library boundaries (MCP's untyped tool arguments).

Reason: basedpyright and zuban were installed but never invoked. Wiring them in surfaced two latent bugs the four invoked checkers all missed — a pyright venv misconfiguration that pyright tolerated silently, and an invariant-list assignment to Textual's BINDINGS that only zuban's mypy-compatible engine flagged. basedpyright is a strict superset of pyright, so running both was the most redundant pairing in the set.

Rejected alternative: relax the strict rules — forfeits the hardening the strict bar drove into the generated code.

Rejected alternative: keep pyright beside basedpyright — pure redundancy.

Consequence: TUI projects gain typing_extensions for @override on 3.10/3.11; ty is pre-release and kept because it currently passes and adds coverage. An earlier zuban miscategorized one finding and forced broadening a mypy disable list; zuban 0.9.0 fixed it and the concession was removed.

docs.title: mypy's prek hook runs through uv, like basedpyright
docs.text:
Id: 71f826cd-950d-4112-9cfb-7dad6ee98264 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: found while adopting the template in openapipages; recorded in ADR-005 (docs/adr/005-five-type-checkers-basedpyright-strict.md) Verification: corroborated — the mirrors-mypy rev (v2.3.0) had drifted from the style group's mypy==2.4.0 pin, and the hook's files = "^src/" skipped the docs/examples path that [tool.mypy] files adds with include_docs Revisit when: mypy needs to run without the project's environment, for example in a hook-only CI job without uv See: architecture-contracts.md#whole-program-analyzers-are-local-system-hooks-backed-by-the-style-group — 41f3397d-1afb-4e57-a0bd-b5ef85089bfc — as of 2026-10-11

The mypy prek hook is a local system hook running mypy from the project's locked style group, with pass_filenames = false.

Reason: the mirrors-mypy hook ran in an isolated venv. It needed a Jinja list in additional_dependencies copying each component's runtime deps, and a missed entry failed only on the adopter's first full hook run. It also carried a second mypy version that Renovate bumped separately from the style pin, and its own file filter. The local hook uses the project's environment, the style pin, and [tool.mypy] files, the same as tox.

Rejected alternative: keep mirrors-mypy and add a test that its additional_dependencies match the runtime deps. That guards one of the three drifts and keeps the duplicate version pin.

docs.title: MegaLinter is an opt-in lean complement, non-blocking on three levels
docs.text:
Id: f3041701-610f-4418-b297-e9707da5de40 Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-013 (docs/adr/013-megalinter-opt-in-lean-complement.md); prompted by a real run (hwid#90) Revisit when: prek gains one of the five enabled linters, the cupcake flavor drops one, or GitHub changes SARIF ingestion rules See: external-integrations.md#a-freshly-generated-project-is-green-on-first-push-with-zero-external-accounts — 392b6dcf-6e9d-441d-bf7b-64ba362578d7 — as of 2026-10-11 See: lint-orchestration.md#the-tox-style-env-is-the-sole-authoritative-lint-suite-prek-is-a-fast-gate-not-a-second-suite — 9b74fc8b-a808-4f2b-bdbd-9e4253c1b35a — as of 2026-10-11

include_megalinter (default off) renders the workflow and config. Enabled linters are only the gaps prek and tox leave: shellcheck for standalone scripts, hadolint (gated on include_web, the only config that renders a Dockerfile), jsonlint, copy-paste detection, and cspell scoped to Markdown as a deeper dictionary pass beside prek's fast typos. It uses the smaller cupcake flavor image, no paths filter, exits 0 (DISABLE_ERRORS), posts no commit status, and is not in the check gate; findings reach the Security tab through a best-effort SARIF upload of the single aggregate report.

Reason: the always-on predecessor was documented nowhere, pulled an ~8 GB image on every push (165 s of a 3-minute run was the pull), and five of its six linters re-ran checks prek already performed. Unlike the external-service integrations it needs no account, so it earned its own decision. A paths filter was tried and dropped: copy-paste detection scans source, so the filter fired on nearly every PR anyway and only confused. Pointing the SARIF upload at the reports directory was rejected because GitHub rejects a file whose runs share a tool and category; the aggregate's per-linter runs carry distinct tool names.

Rejected alternative: always-on — the posture above.

Rejected alternative: drop cspell entirely — an earlier revision did; it was reinstated, scoped, during review.

Consequence: the best-effort upload fails silently, so the SARIF path is verified against a live public repository via the code-scanning API, not by rendering, after any change to that step or a major bump. A project wanting MegaLinter to gate requires its code-scanning results via branch protection.

docs.title: semgrep runs in the style env against a named registry ruleset, never vendored
docs.text:
Id: 5068081c-24ce-4c39-9cdf-13e0a7c229b4 Type: decision Type: constraint Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-032 (docs/adr/032-semgrep-sast-in-the-style-env.md); issue #174 Revisit when: offline determinism outranks rule quality, semgrep gains an on-disk rule cache, or the registry rules' license permits redistribution See: lint-orchestration.md#the-tox-style-env-is-the-sole-authoritative-lint-suite-prek-is-a-fast-gate-not-a-second-suite — 9b74fc8b-a808-4f2b-bdbd-9e4253c1b35a — as of 2026-10-11

semgrep is pinned in its own sast dependency group, runs only in the tox style env over src with the p/python registry pack, findings blocking and telemetry off. It is not a prek hook, not in check-security.yml, and no ruleset is committed.

Reason: the registry rules carry the Semgrep Rules License, which forbids distribution — a Copier template exists to distribute files, so vendoring them is exactly the prohibited act. semgrep keeps no on-disk rule cache, so a prek hook would hit the registry on every commit and fail offline; the style-env-only placement follows the ty/pyrefly/zuban precedent. The dedicated group exists because dev includes style wholesale and the wheel is ~215 MB with a native core; only the Linux style job should pay that. --config auto was avoided so rule selection is reproducible.

Rejected alternative: hand-authored rules — legal and offline, but a hand-maintained taint database catching less than the relevant community rules.

Rejected alternative: a uvx semgrep job in check-security.yml — pure duplication once semgrep is in style, with an unpinned version Renovate did not track.

Consequence: not hermetic — a new community rule or a registry outage can redden an unrelated PR; findings overlap ruff's bandit rules, so a line may need both suppressions. The marginal value is cross-statement taint rules ruff cannot express.

docs.title: Homebrew and Scoop are opt-in dispatches; the tap or bucket owns the manifest logic
docs.text:
Id: 462ac46c-c9db-4a4a-b8ae-bbe5c14af09f Type: decision Status: active Evidence: confirmed Source: ADR-017 (docs/adr/017-opt-in-homebrew-scoop-distribution.md); the live reference is the keycast tap and bucket repositories Revisit when: the release build matrix becomes per-architecture, or an ecosystem's own bump tooling changes shape See: external-integrations.md#a-freshly-generated-project-is-green-on-first-push-with-zero-external-accounts — 392b6dcf-6e9d-441d-bf7b-64ba362578d7 — as of 2026-10-11 See: package-distribution.md#optional-pypi-publishing — 20be7463-ca95-4d01-82c9-71f632d1b4be — as of 2026-10-11

include_homebrew and include_scoop are independent toggles, off by default and asked only when the project can distribute natively. When enabled, release.yml gains bump-homebrew/bump-scoop jobs that fire a repository_dispatch at the owner's homebrew-tap/scoop-bucket repository with only the package name and version.
